facts.statement: The genus Datousaurus was named by Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu in 1984.
facts.quote: Datousaurus was named by Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu in 1984.

facts.statement: Only two partial skeletons of Datousaurus have been discovered to date.
facts.quote: To date, only two partial skeletons have been discovered.

facts.statement: Neither of the two discovered partial skeletons had an articulated skull, though one skull attributed to the genus has been found.
facts.quote: Neither had an articulated skull, although one skull has been discovered that has been attributed to the genus.

facts.statement: The name Datousaurus means "chieftain lizard" or "big-head lizard," derived from a pun on its large head.
facts.quote: Datousaurus (meaning "chieftain lizard" or "big-head lizard"; originally named using the Malay datu, after its Chinese nickname qiulong - literally "chieftain dragon" - but also a pun on its big head; da tou means "big head" in Chinese)

facts.statement: Datousaurus lived in the Middle Jurassic alongside sauropods like Shunosaurus and Omeisaurus, the neornithischian Xiaosaurus, the stegosaur Huayangosaurus, and the carnivore Gasosaurus.
facts.quote: It shared the local Middle Jurassic landscape with other sauropods such as Shunosaurus, Omeisaurus, and Protognathosaurus, the neornithischian Xiaosaurus, and the early stegosaur Huayangosaurus as well as the carnivorous Gasosaurus.

facts.statement: Datousaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur measuring approximately 10 to 13.9 meters in length.
facts.quote: Datousaurus was about 10-13.9 meters long and herbivorous.

facts.statement: Datousaurus possessed a deep and large skull, which is unusual for a sauropod.
facts.quote: It had a deep large skull for a sauropod.

facts.statement: Datousaurus had elongated vertebrae that allowed it to reach higher, and its teeth were spoon-shaped.
facts.quote: Datousaurus's elongated vertebrae gave it a higher reach and its teeth were more spoon shaped.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the different feeding adaptations of Datousaurus and Shunosaurus may indicate they ate different plants or fed at different heights to reduce competition.
facts.quote: This may be a sign that these contemporaries fed on different plants and/or at different heights in the trees.

facts.statement: The rarity of Datousaurus fossils suggests it may not have lived in herds like other sauropods.
facts.quote: The rarity of its fossils suggest that it may not have been as social as other sauropods, which are often preserved in large numbers in a single deposit.

facts.statement: Datousaurus is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.
Datousaurus lived approximately 168 to 162 million years ago during the Bathonian and Callovian stages.
facts.quote: hace aproximadamente 168 a 162 millones de años entre el Bathoniense y el Calloviense

facts.statement: Fossils of Datousaurus were discovered in the lower Shaximiao Formation at Dashanpu in Zigong, Sichuan province, China.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en la región más baja de la Formación Shaximiao en Dashanpu, provincia de Zigong Sichuan, China

facts.statement: Some sources estimate the length of Datousaurus to be nearly 15 meters.
The parent group of the genus Datousaurus is Eusauropoda.
The time range for Datousaurus spans from the Aalenian to the Oxfordian, between 174.7 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Oxfordian (174.7 to 154.8 million years ago)
